_meta.purpose: Historical ground truth for validating the scenario/shock engine. The engine has never been validated against anything; data/scenario_spec.json carries 12 magnitude constants all flagged calibrated:false.
_meta.how_to_read_confidence: Every list carries its own confidence. HIGH = sourced from the cited document. MEDIUM = sourced but a detail (ordering, exact date) may be imprecise. LOW = inferred from general knowledge, NOT verified — these are held OUT of scoring by default until checked against FAO GIEWS or IPC records.
_meta.scoring_rule: POSITIVE episodes score precision@k and recall against expected_hurt_top / expected_responders, always versus a permutation null. NEGATIVE episodes score the opposite question: how loudly did the engine shout about countries that turned out fine (false_alarm_at_10).
_meta.why_negative_episodes_matter: The first-order model ignores substitution and stocks and is estimated to overstate impact 2-4x. The episodes that expose that are the ones where a major exporter withdrew supply and little followed. Scoring only on crises would hide the exact failure mode this engine is suspected of having.

episodes.event: Russia wheat export ban following drought and wildfires
episodes.magnitude_note: ~8 Mt Russian production loss, +2.5 Mt Kazakhstan/Ukraine. World wheat 149 -> 318 USD/t, Jun 2010 - Feb 2011.
episodes.notes: The cascade was NOTABLY SMALL versus 2008 — only Ukraine and Kazakhstan followed. US/EU/Australia backfilled, no global wheat famine, and Egypt paid more but did not run out. An engine predicting a wide cascade here is over-firing.

episodes.event: India non-basmati white rice export ban
episodes.magnitude_note: Non-basmati white + broken rice ~45% of India's 2022 rice exports. FAO rice index reached 142 by Aug 2023, highest since Oct 2011.
episodes.notes: THE MOST VALUABLE FIXTURE. A very large exporter withdrew ~45% of its rice exports and no meaningful cascade followed. expected_responders is deliberately EMPTY — that emptiness is the test. An engine naming a long list of follow-on restrictors here is wrong in the direction it is already suspected of being wrong.

episodes.event: COVID-era export restrictions (Vietnam, Cambodia, Russia, Kazakhstan)
episodes.magnitude_note: Vietnam contract moratorium late Mar 2020 (lifted 1 May); Cambodia ban 5 Apr (lifted 20 May); Russia/Kazakhstan quotas to 30 Jun.
episodes.notes: THE FALSE-POSITIVE EPISODE. Restrictions were real and multi-country, but almost everything reversed within 4-8 weeks, stocks were high, and no major importer deteriorated FROM TRADE POLICY — deterioration came from income loss and logistics, which this engine does not model and must not claim. expected_hurt_top is deliberately empty.

episodes.magnitude_note: Full export ban, widened to crude palm oil, REVOKED after 21 days.
episodes.notes: Price effect, not availability. Duration (21 days) was the decisive variable and the engine has NO concept of duration — a permanent-ban assumption is structurally wrong here. Indonesian FARMERS were the biggest losers (FFB prices -60%), a domestic-incidence effect the engine does not model. Kept precisely because it is a case the engine cannot get right, for reasons worth stating.

episodes.event: Russia-Ukraine war, Black Sea grain disruption
episodes.magnitude_note: Restricting countries rose 3 -> 16 by early April 2022; peak ~23 countries, ~17% of traded calories; 32 countries / 77 measures over 2022.
episodes.notes: Largest cascade in the set and the best positive test. Note the counterfactual: no global famine followed — the Black Sea Grain Initiative (Jul 2022) plus record Australian and Russian harvests pushed wheat BELOW pre-war levels by late 2022. An engine with no concept of policy or supply response will overstate the tail.

episodes.magnitude_note: Attributed contributions to the 61% rice price rise: India 23%, Vietnam 20%, Egypt 10%, China 8%.
episodes.notes: CRITICAL CAVEAT: the physical shortage never existed. Global rice stocks were adequate; this was a policy-and-panic spike, broken partly by Japan's WTO-held rice offer to the Philippines. A structural-exposure engine will attribute it to fundamentals it can see and be right about WHO for the wrong REASON. Score the ranking; do not claim the mechanism.
